sources.evidence: Official feature docs: GitHub Copilot Memory stores two types -- repository-level facts (coding conventions, architectural decisions, build commands) and user-level personal preferences. types.name: Session event envelope (ephemeral vs persisted)
types.lodIdea: The single most direct LOD control found in any source this session: every copilot-sdk event carries ephemeral:true (or absent=false). Ephemeral events (deltas, progress, session.idle, elicitation/user_input/permission... see per-event notes) stream live but are never written to the session log and are NOT replayed on resume; persisted events are durable and replayable. parentId chains only persisted events together.

types.caveat: Public API (official copilot-sdk docs page). Per-event ephemeral/persisted status given in the per-event notes below is as documented on this page; not cross-checked against generated SDK source.

types.lodIdea: assistant.message carries content plus three parallel, provider-specific opaque/plain reasoning fields on the SAME message: reasoningOpaque (Anthropic encrypted thinking), encryptedContent (OpenAI encrypted reasoning), reasoningText (readable reasoning text), plus phase('thinking'|'response'). This is the CLI/SDK-side analogue to VS Code's includeEncryptedThinking flag (T9) -- confirms the opaque-vs-readable reasoning split is a cross-harness, cross-provider concept, not VS Code-specific.

types.caveat: Public API.

types.name: tool.execution_start/progress/shell_output/execution_complete and 3-tier result content
types.lodIdea: tool.execution_complete.result has three explicit LOD tiers at once: content (concise, may be truncated for token efficiency, sent to the LLM), detailedContent (full, preserves complete diffs etc., for display), and contents (ContentBlock[] structured text/terminal/image/audio/resource). tool.shell_output is a 4th, ephemeral, append-only live-terminal channel explicitly NOT persisted/replayed, superseding the deprecated tool.execution_partial_result bounded-snapshot channel.
types.structure: tool.execution_start data:{toolCallId, toolName, arguments?, mcpServerName?, mcpServerDisplayName?, mcpToolName?}; tool.execution_complete data:{toolCallId, success, result?:{content, detailedContent?, contents?:ContentBlock[]}, error?:{message,code?}, toolTelemetry?, isUserRequested?}
types.caveat: Public API. MCP identity resolved as mcpConfigServerName ?? mcpServerName (legacy-compatible) per doc note; ContentBlock[] item shape not itself detailed on this page.

types.name: subagent.started/completed/failed/selected/deselected
types.lodIdea: A fuller subagent lifecycle schema than VS Code's name-only ChatSubagentToolInvocationData (T-gap): started carries agentName/agentDisplayName/agentDescription/model; completed/failed add durationMs/totalTokens/totalToolCalls; selected is an inferred-routing event (no toolCallId) with a tools:string[]|null scope (null = all tools); deselected has an explicitly empty {} payload.
types.structure: subagent.started:{toolCallId,agentName,agentDisplayName,agentDescription,model?}; subagent.completed:{toolCallId,agentName,agentDisplayName,model?,durationMs?,totalTokens?,totalToolCalls?}; subagent.failed: same + error; subagent.selected:{agentName,agentDisplayName,tools:string[]|null}; subagent.deselected:{}
types.caveat: Public API. Envelope-level agentId (T43) is the correlation mechanism for routing sub-agent assistant/tool events to a separate UI lane; parentToolCallId on assistant/tool events is explicitly marked deprecated in favor of agentId.

types.name: skill.invoked
types.lodIdea: Confirms Skills (SKILL.md, T36/T38 gap) are delivered to the model as fully-injected content, not a reference/pointer: content holds the full skill text. allowedTools documents the skill's requested auto-approval scope but the doc is explicit that the SDK does not auto-approve them -- the host's permission handler still decides (CLI auto-approves while active; other hosts may not).
types.structure: data:{name, path, content, allowedTools?:string[], pluginName?, pluginVersion?}
types.caveat: Public API. Resolves part of the earlier SKILL.md gap (event-level shape now known); the SKILL.md frontmatter schema itself is still not directly verified.

types.name: permission.requested/completed (incl. kind:"memory")
types.lodIdea: CORRECTS prior gap framing: GitHub Copilot Memory IS a publicly documented feature (S21), and the SDK's own schema for the write-side of a memory action is this permission kind: {subject, fact, citations}, matching the docs' statement that facts/preferences are cited back to supporting code or quotes. No separate dedicated memory.* event family (e.g. memory.created/memory.retired) was found in this pass -- the approval-flow event is the only memory-adjacent schema documented here. Other kinds (shell/write/read/mcp/url/custom-tool) are the general tool/file/network approval LOD gate; result.kind has 5 named outcomes incl. distinct denied-by-rules vs denied-interactively-by-user vs denied-by-content-exclusion-policy.
types.structure: permission.requested data:{requestId, permissionRequest:{kind:'shell'|'write'|'read'|'mcp'|'url'|'memory'|'custom-tool', ...kind-specific fields, toolCallId?}}; permission.completed data:{requestId, result.kind:'approved'|'denied-by-rules'|'denied-interactively-by-user'|'denied-no-approval-rule-and-could-not-request-from-user'|'denied-by-content-exclusion-policy'}
types.caveat: Public API for the event schema (S22). Whether these events are flagged ephemeral was not explicitly stated on the page (no 'Ephemeral.' marker was present for this section, unlike sibling user_input/elicitation events) -- inferred as persisted by the doc's own convention, not an explicit claim; flag as INFERRED for that specific point.

types.name: user_input.requested/completed and elicitation.requested/completed
types.lodIdea: Two parallel ephemeral ask/answer event pairs: user_input.* for free-text/choice questions the agent itself originates, elicitation.* specifically for MCP's elicitation/create protocol (mode:'form') plus a non-MCP mode:'url' (open a browser URL) -- i.e. the CLI/SDK host renders both agent-native questions and MCP elicitation requests through a related-but-separate event-family, unlike VS Code's single ChatQuestion/ChatResponseQuestionCarouselPart (T-existing) which does not distinguish an MCP origin.
types.structure: user_input.requested:{requestId,question,choices?,allowFreeform?,toolCallId?}; user_input.completed:{requestId,answer?,wasFreeform?}; elicitation.requested:{requestId,message,mode?:'form'|'url',requestedSchema?,url?,elicitationSource?,elicitationSourceDisplayName?,toolCallId?}; elicitation.completed:{requestId,action?:'accept'|'decline'|'cancel',content?}
types.caveat: Public API, both marked Ephemeral. in the source doc.

types.name: Session lifecycle: idle/compaction/usage_info vs usage_checkpoint/shutdown
types.lodIdea: session.usage_info (ephemeral, per-snapshot context-window utilization: tokenLimit/currentTokens/systemTokens/conversationTokens/toolDefinitionsTokens) is explicitly a DIFFERENT, lower-durability tier than session.usage_checkpoint (NOT marked ephemeral; described as a 'Durable aggregate usage checkpoint used to reconstruct accounting when a session is resumed' -- totalNanoAiu, totalPremiumRequests). session.compaction_start/complete brackets context-compaction with a rich result (preCompactionTokens/postCompactionTokens/messagesRemoved/summaryContent/checkpointNumber/checkpointPath). session.shutdown aggregates whole-session metrics (modelMetrics per model, codeChanges linesAdded/linesRemoved/filesModified, totalApiDurationMs).
types.structure: session.idle(ephemeral):{aborted?,mode?}; session.compaction_start(ephemeral):{}; session.compaction_complete:{success,error?,preCompactionTokens?,postCompactionTokens?,preCompactionMessagesLength?,messagesRemoved?,tokensRemoved?,summaryContent?,checkpointNumber?,checkpointPath?,compactionTokensUsed?,requestId?}; session.usage_info(ephemeral):{tokenLimit,currentTokens,messagesLength,systemTokens?,conversationTokens?,toolDefinitionsTokens?,isInitial?}; session.usage_checkpoint:{totalNanoAiu,totalPremiumRequests?}; session.shutdown:{shutdownType:'routine'|'error',errorReason?,totalPremiumRequests?,totalApiDurationMs,sessionStartTime,codeChanges,modelMetrics,currentModel?}
types.caveat: Public API. Directly answers the task's progress + compaction + usage-persisted-vs-ephemeral questions at the CLI/SDK layer.

types.name: assistant.usage (per-API-call usage/cost, ephemeral)
types.lodIdea: Rich, fully field-level public usage schema distinct from, and more granular than, the session-aggregate T52 events: per-call inputTokens/outputTokens/reasoningTokens (subset of outputTokens)/cacheReadTokens/cacheWriteTokens, cost (billing multiplier), duration, timeToFirstTokenMs/interTokenLatencyMs (streaming perf), reasoningEffort, apiEndpoint (incl. distinguishing /chat/completions vs /v1/messages vs /responses vs ws:/responses vs /interactions), quotaSnapshots and copilotUsage (itemized provider cost breakdown), contentFilterTriggered/finishReason.
types.structure: data:{model,inputTokens?,outputTokens?,reasoningTokens?,cacheReadTokens?,cacheWriteTokens?,cacheExpiresAt?,contentFilterTriggered?,finishReason?,cost?,duration?,timeToFirstTokenMs?,interTokenLatencyMs?,reasoningEffort?,initiator?,apiCallId?,serviceRequestId?,apiEndpoint?,providerCallId?,quotaSnapshots?,copilotUsage?}
types.caveat: Public API. Marked Ephemeral.; resolves prior T40 gap (per-call usage fields) at the CLI/SDK layer -- VS Code's own ChatResult usage shape remains separately unverified.

types.name: SerializedChatResponsePart (VS Code internal persisted-history union)
types.lodIdea: The actual on-disk/history-serialization part union is narrower than the live ChatResponseStream part union (vscodeTypes.ts, T-existing): only 9 named members (markdown, file-tree, inline-reference, markdown-with-vulnerability, thinking, a generic serialized-progress-content wrapper, question-carousel, plan-review, disabled-Claude-hooks). This is a concrete, line-cited content-vs-persisted-history LOD narrowing point -- many live-stream part types (confirmation, warning, command-button, etc.) are evidently NOT part of this persisted union by name, implying they are either excluded from history or folded into the generic IChatProgressResponseContentSerialized wrapper (wrapper internals not opened).
types.structure: type SerializedChatResponsePart = IMarkdownString | IChatResponseProgressFileTreeData | IChatContentInlineReference | IChatAgentMarkdownContentWithVulnerability | IChatThinkingPart | IChatProgressResponseContentSerialized | IChatQuestionCarousel | IChatPlanReview | IChatDisabledClaudeHooksPart
types.caveat: INFERRED INTERNAL SOURCE -- workbench-internal (chatModel.ts), not an exported vscode.d.ts public API. Member interfaces themselves (e.g. IChatProgressResponseContentSerialized) not individually opened.

types.name: IToolInvocation / IToolInvocationContext (VS Code internal tool-call request shape)
types.lodIdea: Internal request-side tool-call record carries subAgentInvocationId (subagent UI attribution, explicitly called a stop-gap pending unification with thinking/tool-call-group rendering), preToolUseResult (hook integration point, ties directly to the ChatHookType.PreToolUse hook from the earlier pass), preApproved:ConfirmedReason (lets a host/server-side decision skip the WaitingForConfirmation UI state entirely -- a direct confirmation-LOD bypass), and traceparent/tracestate W3C trace-context fields explicitly forwarded to MCP tool calls as _meta.traceparent per MCP SEP-414 (a concrete, named MCP-spec cross-reference not previously found).
types.structure: IToolInvocation:{callId,toolId,toolSessionResource?,originatingChatResource?,parameters,tokenBudget?,context,chatRequestId?,chatInteractionId?,chatStreamToolCallId?,subAgentInvocationId?,toolSpecificData?,modelId?,userSelectedTools?,selectedCustomButton?,preToolUseResult?,preApproved?,traceparent?,tracestate?}; IToolInvocationContext:{sandboxNetworkRestrictions?,sessionResource,requestId?,workingDirectory?}
types.caveat: INFERRED INTERNAL SOURCE -- workbench-internal, not public API. toolSpecificData member interfaces (IChatTerminalToolInvocationData, IChatSessionTargetData, IChatAutomationConfigurationData, etc.) confirmed to exist by name in this union only, not individually opened (consistent with existing NAME-ONLY caveats elsewhere).

types.name: IToolResult (VS Code internal 3-kind content union)
types.lodIdea: Internal result-side content union has only 3 kinds -- promptTsx (opaque prompt-element JSON, re-stringified for accessibility), text (value:string, optional audience?/title?), data (mimeType+VSBuffer, optional audience?/title?) -- narrower than and differently shaped from the public MCP 5-type content union (text/image/audio/resource/resource_link, S1): image/audio/binary are all folded into kind:data generically by mimeType rather than given distinct kinds. Separately, toolResultDetails.mcpOutput is explicitly 'Raw MCP tool result for MCP App UI rendering' -- i.e. the raw upstream MCP CallToolResult is preserved verbatim alongside the lossier internal 3-kind summary, a documented full-fidelity escape hatch.
types.structure: IToolResult:{content:(IToolResultPromptTsxPart|IToolResultTextPart|IToolResultDataPart)[],toolSpecificData?,toolResultMessage?,toolResultDetails?:IToolResultInputOutputDetails|IToolResultOutputDetails,toolResultError?,toolMetadata?,confirmResults?}; IToolResultTextPart:{kind:'text',value,audience?,title?}; IToolResultDataPart:{kind:'data',value:{mimeType,data:VSBuffer},audience?,title?}; IToolResultInputOutputDetails:{input,inputLanguage?,output,isError?,mcpOutput?}
types.caveat: INFERRED INTERNAL SOURCE -- workbench-internal, not public API. LanguageModelPartAudience (the audience? type) was previously NAME-ONLY (T-gap); its referenced use here is additional but still not a full definition read.

controls: MCP: outputSchema/structuredContent presence is itself an LOD switch -- a tool can offer both a terse text block and a full structured object (S1).
MCP: progress 'total' and 'message' are optional per-notification, a fine/coarse LOD choice per update (S2).
MCP: elicitation requestedSchema is restricted to flat primitives -- a protocol-level LOD ceiling, not a client choice (S3).
VS Code hooks: ChatHookResultKind success/error/warning is a 3-level severity LOD per hook call; stopReason vs systemMessage vs silent success are distinct UI-visibility levels (S8).
VS Code hooks: ChatRequestHooks exposes resolved shell commands (cwd/env/timeout) on the request -- a high-sensitivity LOD axis with no documented redaction opt-out found (GAP).
VS Code reasoning: includeEncryptedThinking is an explicit binary LOD switch (opaque/encrypted vs plain) for carrying reasoning state across requests (S9).

VS Code reasoning: LanguageModelThinkingPart (batch, LM-API side) vs thinkingProgress()/ChatResponseThinkingProgressPart (streaming delta, chat-response side) appear to be two separate LOD channels for the same concept -- existence confirmed, exact relationship not (S7,S9,S10).
VS Code tool auto-approval: documented autoApprove/autopilot spectrum controls confirmation UI (T19) volume per tool call; full enum not captured (GAP).

VS Code auto-routing (fusion-adjacent): ChatAutoModeTier (efficiency/balance/intelligence/fast) + ChatResponseAutoModeResolutionPart give a documented 4-level LOD for which-model-was-picked transparency, repeatable per turn (S10).
VS Code history LOD: ChatResponseTurn2.response explicitly excludes metadata-only stream parts, a documented content/metadata split for persisted history (S11).

Hooks are explicitly NOT portable across harnesses (Local vs Copilot vs Claude vs Codex each have distinct hook schema/location) despite shared file-naming conventions -- an LOD/compatibility trap called out directly in docs (S19).

Agent Plugins 1.0 draws an explicit standard-vs-client-specific line: Skills and MCP servers are portable; Agents, Hooks, Automation templates, Slash commands are client-specific under com.github.copilot -- a documented LOD/portability boundary (S18).

copilot-sdk event envelope: the ephemeral boolean flag (T43) is the SDK's single clearest, explicit LOD control -- it is the documented switch between live-only/non-replayable detail and durable/replayable detail, applied consistently across assistant/tool/session/permission/elicitation event families (S22).

copilot-sdk tool results: a documented 3-tier LOD per tool call -- content (concise, token-efficient, LLM-facing, may be truncated) vs detailedContent (full, display-facing) vs contents (structured ContentBlock[]) -- gives an explicit, named precedent for a text/detailed/structured LOD split (S22, T47).

copilot-sdk usage: two separate durability tiers for cost/usage data -- session.usage_info (ephemeral, per-snapshot context-window view) vs session.usage_checkpoint (durable, resume-reconstructable aggregate) vs assistant.usage (ephemeral, full per-call billing/perf detail) -- a 3-way usage LOD split, more granular than anything found on the VS Code extension-API side (S22, T52, T53).

copilot-sdk permission.completed.result.kind enumerates 5 distinct approval/denial outcomes (approved, denied-by-rules, denied-interactively-by-user, denied-no-approval-rule-and-could-not-request-from-user, denied-by-content-exclusion-policy) -- a finer confirmation-outcome LOD than the 3-tier ChatHookResultKind found earlier (S22, T50).

VS Code internal: preApproved:ConfirmedReason on IToolInvocation is a documented mechanism for skipping the confirmation UI state entirely when a decision was already resolved out-of-band (e.g. agent-host server-side auto-approval) -- a concrete confirmation-LOD bypass distinct from the public autoApprove/autopilot spectrum (S24, T55).

VS Code internal: toolResultDetails.mcpOutput explicitly preserves the raw upstream MCP CallToolResult verbatim alongside the lossier internal 3-kind IToolResult.content summary -- a documented full-fidelity escape hatch co-existing with a lower-LOD default summary (S24, T56).
gaps: Memory (UPDATED): GitHub Copilot Memory IS a publicly documented feature (S21: repository-level facts + user-level preferences, cited, 28-day auto-expiry) and the copilot-sdk documents an event-level schema for the write/approval side (S22, T50: permission.requested kind:"memory" = {subject,fact,citations}). Remaining gap: no dedicated persisted memory.* event family (e.g. memory.created/retired) was found distinct from the approval flow, and the underlying storage/retrieval/similarity-matching mechanism is not documented at a schema level in any source read.
Custom instructions page and SKILL.md frontmatter schema (agent-plugins.org) were referenced but not fetched -- exact field-level LOD controls unknown (T36,T38).
ChatResult's own field list was not opened; any usage/telemetry/cost fields on a chat result are unverified (T40).

ChatToolInvocationPart, ChatMcpToolInvocationData, McpToolInvocationContentData, LanguageModelToolMCPSource, LanguageModelToolExtensionSource, ChatResponseReferencePart/2, ChatResponseWarningPart, ChatResponseInfoPart, ChatErrorLevel, ChatResponseProgressPart2, ChatResponseVoiceProgressStage, Notebook/Workspace/ExternalEditPart class bodies confirmed to exist by name only -- NAME-ONLY/PARTIAL, not verified API shape.
microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat is archived (S13); its historical file tree was not re-opened to diff pre-archival public API vs current extensions/copilot-in-monorepo surface.

The openai/codex git component pinned in cgmanifest.json (S6) is a dependency/license-inventory record only (corrected framing) -- it does not establish which runtime executes Copilot turns or the extension's full successor history; its functional role in the running extension was not explored further and remains UNKNOWN, not merely INFERRED.

MCP spec pages for Sampling, Roots, Prompts, Resources (beyond fragments on the Tools page) were not individually fetched; S17 claims about MCP deprecating Sampling/Roots not cross-verified against MCP's own wording.

Follow-up: github/copilot-sdk docs/features/streaming-events.md (S22) was fetched directly as a primary source and is now cited extensively (T43-T53). This is a hand-maintained reference page, not the generated SessionEvent union/type source itself -- the page explicitly states it does not cover every event type and that the generated per-language union is the authoritative exhaustive list; that generated schema file was not opened in this bounded follow-up.

ChatResponseAutoModeResolutionPart/ChatAutoModeTier (T28) is the closest analogue found to model-fusion; no multi-model ensembling/voting/fusion mechanism was found documented anywhere checked -- may not exist publicly, or exists under different terminology not yet located.

VS Code internal chatModel.ts/languageModelToolsService.ts citations (S23,S24; T54-T56) are INFERRED INTERNAL SOURCE, not public extension API -- useful for understanding current persisted-history/tool-result shape, but these types are not part of vscode.d.ts and may change without any public API deprecation notice.

interpretationNotes.finding: Input, result and attachment detail need separate controls
interpretationNotes.evidence: SDK documentation describes result.content, detailedContent and contents, while MCP supports text/image/audio/resource/resource_link plus structuredContent.
interpretationNotes.implication: A tool's concise model-facing text is not necessarily its full display result. A no-results choice must also govern newly generated result companions.

interpretationNotes.finding: Ephemeral is an availability boundary, not a way to restore past output
interpretationNotes.evidence: The SDK reference marks live-only event families, including user-input/elicitation and shell-output channels.
interpretationNotes.implication: An offline export can select only what was recorded. Do not promise complete historical questions, live deltas or per-call usage merely because the live API defines them.

interpretationNotes.finding: Question/answer output deserves a semantic category
interpretationNotes.evidence: Local questionCarousel state, agent-native user_input events, MCP elicitation and tool-based ask_user use different records. The Local stress example has an unmatched recorded answer string despite a general verification pass.
interpretationNotes.implication: Short form should keep title plus recorded outcome. Show skipped/cancelled/unavailable separately. A string nonmatch is a warning, not conclusive proof of why content is missing.

interpretationNotes.finding: Memory is a documented feature, but not one export format
interpretationNotes.evidence: GitHub documents repository memories and user preferences. The SDK reference separately describes memory-related permission data.
interpretationNotes.implication: Distinguish a memory operation from loaded instructions, graph queries and compaction. Historical content must come from recorded evidence, not today's memory state.

interpretationNotes.finding: A top-level type union does not prove which content is absent
interpretationNotes.evidence: The checked VS Code SerializedChatResponsePart union includes a generic serialized-progress wrapper whose member definitions were not all opened.
interpretationNotes.implication: The nine top-level members are not nine total persisted kinds. Do not infer that tools, confirmations or warnings cannot persist. The Local survey directly encounters multiple such kinds.

interpretationNotes.finding: Public documentation and sampled private events have different coverage
interpretationNotes.evidence: The survey sees Fusion, usage_record, skill reference, model snapshot and hook events beyond the verified public event subset. Public Auto routing is not evidence that Fusion is model ensembling.
interpretationNotes.implication: Keep unfamiliar event reporting independent of content filters. The report inventories observed names without inventing undocumented semantics.

interpretationNotes.finding: Dependency inventories do not establish which runtime executed a chat
interpretationNotes.evidence: The online pass records a Codex component entry and a changing VS Code extension layout.
interpretationNotes.implication: These are background source observations. They neither broaden this exporter's provider scope nor establish Copilot runtime behavior. Claude/Codex sessions remain out of scope.
